_about: Effects data (Track X, scripts/fx/): damage smoke and the three-phase crash (mid-air explosion, out of control, ground impact). EVERY VALUE IS A PROPOSED VALUE RECORD {value, _proposed, _reason}, made 2026-10-09; none is a decision until Alex chooses from variants/damage-smoke/ and variants/crash-explosion/ and the choice is recorded in data/decisions/decisions.json. Decisions in force it obeys: particles are designed in style, FAST FLASHES WITH A VERY SLOW DECAY (Alex); everything is ink on parchment; shadow strength 0.44; pen 'shadow side'; a plane's shadow falls as if it flew at 1% of its altitude and its gap follows the drawn size. 2026-10-10, Track X2 (the strike): flak, bomb and ruin sections and their roles were added, all proposed, for variants/flak/, variants/bomb-impact/ and variants/tower-ruin/.

accents._about: The effects' extra base colours, in OKLCH beside the two side accents of data/params/render_defaults.json (side_a oklch(0.551 0.100 30), side_b oklch(0.551 0.100 260), equal lightness and chroma, Alex). INTERIM (2026-10-10): Alex rejected the first fire colour, oklch(0.72 0.14 56), as cartoony (round-1 crash board); until he picks from the fire research (docs/proposals/fire-in-ink.md) the working values are that document's treatment 6, 'knock-out + scorch edge'. EVERY ONE OF THESE IS A PROPOSED WORKING VALUE, NOT A DECISION. The principles it follows: the flash is the lightest value on the map (light is the paper), colour is a quiet earth on the paper-ink axis at or below the sides' chroma and lives only in the first tenths of a second and the embers, cooling goes to grey-brown and ink, never to pastel.

oklch._reason: INTERIM working value, proposed (fire research, treatment 6 and 1): the knock-out flash step, paper plus 0.12 in lightness with chroma eased to 0.016, lighter than every fill, no new hue; also the 'white' of the plain smoke of damage-smoke-r2

UNUSED while fire_switch.enabled is false (Alex 2026-10-10: no fire for now). INTERIM working value, PROPOSED, pending Alex's fire pick (not a decision): the scorch of the fire research's treatment 6, a raw-sienna earth on the paper-ink hue axis (ink hue 69, dirt 76), chroma 0.085 below the sides' 0.100, lightness a step on the ramp between paper and dirt, 0.162 from brick red in OKLab; replaces the rejected orange oklch(0.72 0.14 56), which round 1's crash board shows. Used only at the hot edge for the first few tenths of a second, in flame tongues and in embers

UNUSED while fire_switch.enabled is false. INTERIM working value, PROPOSED, pending Alex's fire pick (not a decision): the cooling step of the fire research's treatment 6, a grey-brown on the same axis; the burst hands over to it, then to ink stipple and the smoke

fire_switch._about: THE FIRE MACHINERY'S SWITCH. Alex 2026-10-10: 'No fire for now. Just smoke.' With enabled false (the working value) nothing of fire is made or drawn: no flash, no fireball, no flame on a falling plane, no embers; a mid-air explosion and a ground crash are smoke events (a quick thick burst of smoke that casts a shadow, debris pieces, then smoke that cools and thins very slowly; on the ground the wreck and its scar with a smoke column), and an out-of-control plane trails heavy smoke without a flame. The fire code stays, behind this switch, for a later fire round: turn it on and the interim values in `accents` (the fire research's treatment 6) are what it draws.

enabled._decided: Alex 2026-10-10: 'No fire for now. Just smoke.' (replacing the first orange, rejected as cartoony, and the interim treatment-6 values, which stay in the data unused)
enabled._reason: Alex's decision, recorded in data/decisions/decisions.json as fire-colour (chosen: no fire for now, just smoke)

roles._about: Every colour the effects draw, as a palette role (working rule 6; docs/proposals/palette-architecture.md). base is a colour of data/params/render_defaults.json (paper, ink, object_fill, wall_fill, rock_fill, roof_lit, dirt, shadow = the chosen tint, side_a, side_b) or `fire`, the effects' accent defined below; toward + t mixes toward another palette colour; shade names one of the palette's own shadow-mix fractions (roof_shaded_shadow_mix 0.42, wall_slope_shadow_mix 0.30) and mixes the shadow tint in by it; alpha is a number (the palette's alpha steps: stipple 0.55, rings 0.88, dirt 0.15-0.40) or the name of a render parameter. Resolved in the order toward, shade, alpha by scripts/fx/fx_style.gd. ALL PROPOSED (Track X, 2026-10-09).

smoke._about: Damage smoke (Alex 2026-10-09: 'damage smoke and crash explosions'). A damaged plane trails puffs along its flight path; they stay in the world at the plane's altitude, drift, and fade slowly over turns. Four proposed options for Alex's board (variants/damage-smoke/); NONE IS CHOSEN. Intensity = floor + (1 - floor) x (1 - health fraction), none at full health.

form._reason: lobes built like the tree generator's: scallop outline, fill, rings

variants._reason: baked puffs per tone; a trail picks among them so no two neighbours repeat

radius_frac._reason: puff radius as a fraction of the plane's size_m at intensity 0 and 1 (a 9 m fighter: 1.8 to 4.5 m): drawn at the plane's own scale like the plane

interval_s._reason: seconds between puffs at intensity 0 and 1; at 100 m/s a puff every 40 m (a wisp) to every 10 m (a solid trail)

life_s._reason: seconds a puff lasts at intensity 0 and 1: about 5 turns for a wisp, 8 for a heavy trail ('slow decay over turns', Alex's fast flash / very slow decay)

grow._reason: scale at birth and at death: the puff swells as it hangs

grow_tau._reason: how fast it swells, as a share of its life: it takes most of its growth in the first fifth

hold._reason: share of the life at full strength before the slow fade starts

fade_power._reason: how the fade bends: above 1 it lingers, then goes

alpha_steps._reason: empty: the fade is continuous; a list: the fade in those alpha steps only

intensity_floor._reason: the first lost pip already shows a thin trail; the last pip a heavy one

tone_edges._reason: intensity at which the puff steps to the middle and to the heavy tone

wind_mps._reason: a steady drift in world metres per second (x east, y south): smoke drifts a little

wind_jitter_mps._reason: per-puff spread of that drift, so a trail does not slide as one sheet

ground_shadow._reason: whether a puff casts a shadow on the ground by the altitude rule (1% of its height, away from the sun)

tail_frac._reason: where the smoke leaves the plane, as a share of its size behind its centre

lobes_min._reason: outer lobes round the centre (the tree has 3-7)

lobe_d._reason: lobe offset from the centre, as a share of the puff radius (the tree's 0.36)

lobe_r._reason: lobe radius as a share of the puff radius (the tree's 0.34)

crown_r._reason: the crown lobe on top (the tree's 0.48)

lobe_amp._reason: cusp depth of a lobe's scallop: softer than a tree's 0.13, so smoke is rounder than foliage

lobe_amp_var._reason: random addition to the cusp depth

scallop_base._reason: scallops round a lobe = max(5, round(base + R / div)); the tree's is 4.5 + R/3

outline_weight_of._reason: the render_defaults linework multiplier the outline takes: the tree's outline weight

outline_scale._reason: extra multiplier on that weight

outline_ref_px._reason: a puff of this radius (px) takes the full outline weight; a smaller one takes proportionally less, so a tiny puff is not all outline

outline_min_scale._reason: the least a small puff's outline weight is scaled to

outline_union._reason: wash form only: one outline round the merged silhouette instead of every lobe's

underside._reason: a shadow-tint underside on the side away from the light (the proposed treatment)

lit_shift._reason: the lit part's offset toward the light as a share of the lobe radius; the crescent left is the underside

ticks._reason: short cusp ticks toward the centre, as on a tree

stipple_per_r._reason: stipple dots on the shadow side per px of lobe radius (the tree's 0.6)

rings._reason: nested broken contour rings per lobe (the tree has 3)

ring_role._reason: ring colour role

dash_px._reason: length of a dash of a dashed ring line, px

gap_px._reason: length of the gap between dashes, px

ring_amp._reason: cusp depth of a contour ring's scallop (0 draws a smooth circle); the tree's rings use 0.15

ring_amp_var._reason: random addition to the ring's cusp depth

stages._reason: age stages a puff is baked in: with more than one its rings thin and break as it ages (round 2)

stage_edges._reason: age fractions of the life at which a puff steps to its next stage

stage_ring_keep._reason: by stage: the share of ring segments (or dashes, or arcs) still drawn; the same draw at every stage, so a segment that goes stays gone

stage_ring_alpha._reason: by stage: the ring lines' strength

stage_outline_keep._reason: by stage: the share of the closed outline still drawn (the rest is gaps)

stretch._reason: 1: round puffs; above 1 the puff is drawn longer along the way it was flying (and turned to it), so a trail reads as a moving band (round 2)

shadow_min_tone._reason: the lightest tone that casts a ground shadow when ground_shadow is on: 1 = medium and heavy smoke do, thin does not (Alex 2026-10-10: thick smoke casts one)

arcs_min._reason: open-arc form: the fewest arcs in a puff

arcs_max._reason: open-arc form: the most arcs in a puff

arc_sweep_deg._reason: open-arc form: how far round the circle an arc goes, degrees [least, most]; never 360, so it never closes

arc_spiral._reason: open-arc form: how far an arc's radius drifts along its length (a swirl, not a circle)

arc_weight._reason: open-arc form: line weight multiplier on the tree's inner-ring weight

peak_alpha._reason: the most opaque a puff of this set gets (1 = the option's own strength); the layer's derived sets for the crash's burst, plume, column and trail take burst_alpha here

burst_alpha._reason: the strength this option's puffs take in a DENSE crash burst, plume or column, where many puffs overlap: 1 for an opaque fill; below 1 for a translucent wash, so ten washes do not pile up into a dark blot

arc_jitter._reason: open-arc form: how far an arc's centre may sit from the puff's, as a share of the puff radius

soft_steps._reason: soft form: the number of stepped washes

soft_core._reason: soft form: the smallest wash's size as a share of the cloud's

crash._about: The crash in three phases (Alex 2026-10-09: 'Dead planes should either explode mid air or lose control by players and crash eventually'). The sim rolls a downed plane's fate: EXPLODED (down event, fate exploded: a burst at the plane's altitude, debris, smoke left in the sky) or OUT_OF_CONTROL (the sim flies a descending spiral over turns, then a crash event: a burst on the ground, a plume, a scar). The fall's path and height come from World.sample; the effects draw what rides on it: trail smoke, flame, embers, and the shadow gap closing on the plane's own shadow (the marker layer's). Four proposed options, each one consistent treatment of all three phases, for Alex's board (variants/crash-explosion/); NONE IS CHOSEN.

A._note: The art plan's proposed treatment throughout. Mid-air: a knock-out disc with a scorch rim, short radial hatch and flung ink stipple, then lobed smoke left in the sky; pieces fall with shadows closing on them. Out of control: a heavy lobed trail and a small flame, embers shed. Impact: the same burst with a ring of dust dots, a billow, then a wreck (fuselage, wings, engine, tail on dirt-stipple scorch with ink hatch) that keeps smoking for about twelve turns: a lobed column thinning from heavy grey to a wisp, a few scorch embers on the scar in the first turn.

flak._about: THE FLAK BURST (Track X2, 2026-10-10; Alex: the target is a radio tower, two anti-aircraft batteries fire flak). A shell bursts in the air where it meets or misses a plane: a fast flash and a slowly fading dark puff at the burst's height with its shadow by the altitude rule; hits and misses differ. No fire. ALL OPTIONS ARE PROPOSED; none is chosen (board: variants/flak/).

F1._note: PROPOSED. A flak burst is a dark soft cloud, built the way the soft white smoke is (stepped translucent washes, no outline, the map shows through) in the palette's ink instead of white, so it cannot be mistaken for damage smoke. A fast flash first: a ragged knock-out disc (the lightest step of the palette, no fire) with ink hatch rays and flung dots, a heavier flash and fragments on a hit. The cloud then hangs a few turns, lightening as it ages. Thick enough to cast a shadow by the altitude rule.

end_s._reason: the flipbook is shown until this age (seconds); what remains after it is the smoke, the pit and the pieces

radius_frac._reason: the size as a fraction of the thing's own scale (the burst size, the blast radius, or the tower's size_m)

hit_scale._reason: a hit's flash is this much larger than a miss's

core_curve._reason: the knock-out disc's radius over its age, as a fraction of the flash radius

ruin._about: THE DESTROYED RADIO TOWER (Track X2, 2026-10-10; Alex accepted 'a ruin, crater and smoke column, no fire, from a board'): the moment, the collapse, and what stays, drawn from the unit sheet's own tower model so the ruin is made of the tower's parts. Sizes in metres (the tower is 12 m by the sim). No fire. ALL OPTIONS ARE PROPOSED; none is chosen (board: variants/tower-ruin/).

R1._note: PROPOSED. The tower is blown at its foot and the mast TOPPLES: the same lattice as the standing tower (the unit sheet's) tips over about its base through eight drawn angles in 1.6 s, a second burst of dust where it lands, then it lies broken in two places, members snapped and missing, the platform at the far end. What stays at the foot: a scorched blot with a crater, the four footings cracked and shifted (one gone), leg stumps bent outward, the hut roofless with a torn roof across the hole, the cable snapped. A thick column of the damage smoke rises from the base for about eighteen turns, thinning and greying.
